rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for deliberately deceiving or fooling someone.

example.english: They always kid people by claiming they can read feng shui.
example.traditional: 佢成日呃人，話自己識睇風水。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 ngaak1 jan4 waa6 zi6 gei2 sik1 tai2 fung1 seoi2

rows.note: Use this when asking or accusing someone of messing with you, as in “Are you kidding me?”.

example.english: Are you trying to kid me? I clearly saw you here.
example.traditional: 你玩我呀？我明明見到你喺度㗎喎。
example.jyutping: nei5 waan2 ngo5 aa3 ngo5 ming4 ming4 gin3 dou2 nei5 hai2 dou6 gaa3 wo3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial word for a child or young person.

example.english: That kid is always playing football in the park.
example.traditional: 嗰個細路仔成日喺公園踢波。
example.jyutping: go2 go3 sai3 lou6 zai2 seng4 jat6 hai2 gung1 jyun2 tek3 bo1

rows.note: Use this for simply joking rather than seriously stating something.

example.english: I only kid around, so you don't have to take it so seriously.
example.traditional: 我只係講笑，你唔使咁認真。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zi2 hai6 gong2 siu3 nei5 m4 sai2 gam3 jing6 zan1

rows.note: Use this for someone's son or daughter, especially when referring to their children as a family relationship.

example.english: My kid has already moved out.
example.traditional: 我個仔女已經搬咗出去住喇。
example.jyutping: ngo5 go3 zai2 neoi2 ji5 ging1 bun1 zo2 ceot1 heoi3 zyu6 laa3

rows.note: Use this specifically for a young goat, rather than for a human child.

example.english: The kid is still following its mother around.
example.traditional: 隻山羊仔仲跟住阿媽周圍行。
example.jyutping: zek3 saan1 joeng4 zai2 zung6 gan1 zyu6 aa3 maa1 zau1 wai4 haang4
